question.text: When 2-butyne is treated with $\mathrm{H}_2$ /Lindlar's catalyst, compound $\mathrm{X}$ is produced as the major product and when treated with $\mathrm{Na}$ /liq. $\mathrm{NH}_3$ it produces $\mathrm{Y}$ as the major product. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Y will have higher dipole moment and higher boiling point than $\mathrm{X}$ Y
$\mathrm{Y}$ will have higher dipole moment and lower boiling point than $\mathrm{X}$
X will have lower dipole moment and lower boiling point than $\mathrm{Y}$
$\mathrm{X}$ will have higher dipole moment and higher boiling point than Y

solution.text: When 2-butyne is treated with $\mathrm{H}_2$ /Lindlar's catalyst, compound $\mathrm{X}$ (cis-2-butene) is produced as the major product; and when treated with $\mathrm{Na} /$ liq $\mathrm{NH}_3$ it produces $\mathrm{Y}$ (trans -2- butene) as the major product. Cisisomer $(\mathrm{X})$ will have higher dipole moment and higher boiling point than $\operatorname{trans}(\mathrm{Y})$.
